---
title: MCP server
description: Give a coding agent Teire's scan and catalog, so it checks the repository it is editing and looks up a provider's deprecations before it writes code against them.
icon: Plug
---

`teire mcp` serves Teire's tools over stdio. The protocol uses stdout, and logs go to stderr.

If your agent uses skills, you can also [install the Teire Agent Skill](/docs/build/agent-skill) with `npx skills add teire-dev/teire --skill teire-cli`. The skill teaches the CLI workflow; connecting MCP gives the agent Teire's live tools.

<Tabs items={["Claude Code", "Other clients"]}>
<Tab value="Claude Code">

```bash
claude mcp add teire -- npx -y teire-cli mcp
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Other clients">

Cursor, Windsurf and other clients take the same command in their MCP config:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "teire": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "teire-cli", "mcp"] } } }
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Tools

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `scan_path` | `path` (a folder, or a public GitHub repository as `owner/name` or its URL), optional `fresh` | The groups that need action, one per pull request Teire would open: verdict, priority, deadline, the version or model to move to and the first call sites. The rest are counted. Results are kept 5 minutes per path, unless `fresh` |
| `explain_finding` | `path`, `key` (a group key, change ID or package name) | One group in full: its change records with summary, replacement, migration notes and quoted sources, and up to 50 call sites with their code, product code first |
| `list_changes` | optional `provider`, `ecosystem`, `kind`, `subject` | Changes from the public catalog, or read on the spot from a provider's pages when the catalog doesn't hold them yet: ID, title, kind, class, date and replacement, 60 at a time |
| `get_change` | `id` | One full catalog change record. For a package change computed during a scan, use `explain_finding` instead |

Every tool is marked read-only. None of them writes to the repository or to GitHub. A large repository takes a minute or two to scan; when the client asks for progress, each step is sent as a progress notification, which also keeps clients that reset their timeout on progress from giving up.

## What an agent does with it

- **Before an upgrade:** call `scan_path` on the repository, then `explain_finding` on what it reports. The agent gets the lines to change and the change record: the computed API diff for a package, or the provider's quoted notice for a model or API change.
- **Before writing model code:** call `list_changes` with `provider: "openai"` (or any provider) to see which model IDs are retired or retiring, and what replaces them.
- **In review:** call `get_change` on an ID from a Teire PR for the full record.
